description:
TerraSense is an agricultural decision-support tool that uses NASA Earth observations to help growers improve soil health and rotations. 

Within a web-based visualization platform, crops are recommended based on analysis of geospatial maps showing soil moisture, vegetation, and environmental risks while yields and climate forecasts are offered for sustainable water and soil management and resilient crop rotations.
summary: Farmers are taking TerraSense to improve crop rotations ET, and water use from NASA Earth Observation, soil, and terrain data. TerraSense is an interactive 3D management-zone map, and a 24-month crop-rotation planner. Farmers design and rank rotation plans based on a physics-based water-balance model + machine learning-predicted soil moisture and stress (with uncertainty bands), with settings for equipment, irrigation, prices, and risk aversion evaluated in normal, wet, and dry conditions. Validated in leakage-free spatial and temporal splits.
details:
TerraSense Project Description

WHAT IT DOES AND HOW IT WORKS

TerraSense is a farmer decision-support web platform that connects NASA Earth Observation data with local soil and terrain conditions in an interactive 2.5D/3D management-zone map and a 24-month crop-rotation planner (a 12-month look-back plus a 12-month outlook).

  1. Field Zoning: Any parcel (bounding box or GeoJSON polygon) is divided into an N×N micro-zone grid (3×3 up to 10×10), anchored to USDA SSURGO soil properties and 30 m SRTM DEM terrain derivatives through inverse-distance weighting.
  2. Earth Observation and Hybrid ML Simulation: Daily weather data from NASA POWER feeds a physics-based FAO-56 water-balance backbone, combined with a monotonic LightGBM residual model trained on soil moisture datasets from MERRA-2 (GWETROOT, EVLAND) and ERA5-Land over central Iowa. For each zone and month, the system predicts the Soil Moisture Index (SMI), the Evaporative Stress Index (ESI), evapotranspiration, and proxy indicators of bare-soil and vegetation risk, accompanied by P10 and P90 conformal uncertainty intervals.
  3. Custom Rotation Planning and Ranking: Farmers set constraints and priorities in the web app, such as previous crop, continuous-corn history, equipment (cover-crop drill, no-till drill, hay baler, variable-rate), excluded crops, irrigation cap and cost, commodity and nitrogen prices, and risk aversion. TerraSense then screens the crop plans and ranks the strategies across nominal, dry-analog and wet-analog weather scenarios.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

Actionable Sub-Field Clarity: TerraSense converts broad satellite and reanalysis climate data into an easy-to-understand “Civilization-style” 3D tile grid that shows which sections of a field experience water stress, heat stress, or bare-soil erosion risk, and when those conditions occur.

Risk-Aware Rotation Decisions: Farmers can evaluate trade-offs among net margin, water demand, soil organic matter gain, and operational complexity (such as additional field passes) before finalizing seed and equipment plans for the season.

Resilient and Accessible Design: The platform runs out of the box with no API keys required. Setting TERRASENSE_LIVE=1 pulls live NASA POWER data, and the system automatically falls back to heuristics if the ML artifacts are unavailable.

TOOLS, LANGUAGES AND SOFTWARE USED

Backend and Geospatial ML: Python, Flask, LightGBM, scikit-learn, XGBoost, NumPy, Pandas, Rasterio, dbfread, joblib, pytest.

Frontend and 3D Visualization: Next.js 14 (App Router), TypeScript, React 18, Tailwind CSS, React Three Fiber and Three.js.

Datasets: NASA POWER and MERRA-2, NASA SRTM 1-arc-second DEM (Earthdata), ECMWF ERA5-Land (accessed via Open-Meteo), USDA NRCS SSURGO, ISRIC SoilGrids, and USDA NASS Cropland Data Layer (CDL).

WHAT MAKES IT CREATIVE

Game-Inspired Spatial UX: Instead of spreadsheets and GIS layers, farmers get a 2.5D/3D isometric parcel viewer, a 24-month timeline scrubber, and real-time climate what-if sliders (temp_shift and precip_factor).

Physics, ML and Agronomy Separation: TerraSense combines physical water-balance equations with monotonic-constrained machine learning, so warmer or drier scenarios never produce physically impossible wetter outcomes. Farmer economic and equipment rules sit in a separate, transparent decision layer rather than inside a black box.

KEY FACTORS CONSIDERED

Honest, Leakage-Free Validation: The model is tested with spatial clusters buffered by at least 25 km and with rollouts on unseen years. The ML engine becomes the default only when it outperforms the persistence, climatology, and heuristic baselines.
